questions.questionText: hour 15 minutes Additional Materials: Multiple Choice Answer Sheet Soft clean eraser Soft pencil (type B or HB is recommended) READ THESE INSTRUCTIONS FIRST Write in soft pencil. Do not use staples, paper clips, glue or correction fluid. Write your name, centre number and candidate number on the Answer Sheet in the spaces provided unless this has been done for you. DO NOT WRITE IN ANY BARCODES. There are thirty questions on this paper. Answer all questions. For each question there are four possible answers A, B, C and D. Choose the one you consider correct and record your choice in soft pencil on the separate Answer Sheet. Read the instructions on the Answer Sheet very carefully. Each correct answer will score one mark. A mark will not be deducted for a wrong answer. Any rough working should be done in this booklet.

questions.questionText: The production of a good creates a constant marginal external cost at all levels of output. What value of price elasticity of demand for the good will cause the greatest deadweight welfare loss from the externality?

options.B: equal to one
options.C: greater than one

questions.questionText: What arises in situations where there are costs or benefits associated with a transaction that are not fully reflected in market prices?

options.B: allocative inefficiency
options.C: productive efficiency

options.B: marginal utility X × price of X = marginal utility Y marginal utility X marginal utility Y

questions.questionText: What would explain an increase in the size of an industry and a fall in the average output of the firms in an industry?

options.A: an advance in communication methods which reduce coordination problems within firms
options.B: an advance in technology which increases the cost advantage of capital-intensive methods of production
options.C: an increase in barriers to entry into the industry combined with an increase in barriers to exit from the industry
options.D: an increase in external economies of scale combined with a decrease in internal economies of scale

questions.questionText: Which characteristic would make it easier for firms in an industry to collude?

options.B: homogenous products
options.C: low barriers to entry

options.C: 400000 zero

questions.questionText: Wages in industry X are significantly higher than in industry Y. What could explain this difference?

options.A: Workers in industry Y are highly mobile.
options.B: Trade union organisation in industry Y is relatively strong.
options.C: Industries X and Y compete with each other for workers.

questions.questionText: Good X is a popular product that creates a negative externality when it is consumed. Good Y is a more expensive substitute for X with fewer negative externalities when consumed. The government wants to reduce the consumption of good X significantly but it does not wish to increase its budget deficit. Under which circumstances is the government most likely to meet its aim? government government price elasticity price elasticity subsidises taxes producers of demand for of demand for producers of good X good X good Y of good Y
Which changes in direct and indirect tax are likely to increase the inequality in the distribution of income in a developed economy? direct taxes indirect taxes

options.B: fall rise
options.C: rise fall

questions.questionText: A city has a problem with litter on its streets. The city council is considering several measures to reduce the litter. Which measure to reduce litter would involve the use of ‘nudge’ theory?

options.A: banning the dropping of litter with heavy fines for people who ignore the ban
options.B: installing signs directing people to new litter bins and thanking them for using the bins
options.C: raising local tax and using the money to employ more people to pick up litter
options.D: removing all litter bins so that people have to take their litter home

questions.questionText: The government wants to regulate the consumption of a demerit good in order to increase society’s net welfare. In which situation will society’s net welfare increase?

options.A: The fall in the marginal social benefit is greater than the fall in the marginal social cost.
options.B: The fall in the marginal social cost is greater than the fall in the marginal social benefit.
options.C: The fall in the total social benefit is greater than the fall in the total social cost.
options.D: The fall in the total social cost is greater than the fall in the total social benefit.

questions.questionText: ‘The United Nations Development Programme states that economic growth and development will not reduce poverty, improve equality, generate jobs and secure livelihoods unless it is inclusive and sustainable.’ What would it mean if sustainable economic growth were achieved?

options.A: Countries would benefit equally from growth in the global economy.
options.B: Employees in a country would receive the same growth in incomes.
options.C: Future citizens would benefit from economic growth and development.
options.D: Producers in a country would experience the same growth in demand.

questions.questionText: The table shows information about employment in a country. numbers unemployment year employed rate(%) 2012 10m 2 2017 11m 10 What can be concluded from the table about the country in the period 2012 to 2017?

options.B: The number of job vacancies fell.
options.C: The participation rate fell.

questions.questionText: Which type of unemployment results from industrial reorganisation due to technological change?

options.B: frictional unemployment
options.C: seasonal unemployment

questions.questionText: During a year, a country’s national income in money terms increased by 5%, prices increased by 4% and the total population increased by 2%. What was the approximate change in real income per head?

options.B: a decrease of 2%
options.C: an increase of 1%

questions.questionText: Commercial banks in a country hold $50 million in cash but have created $600 million deposits. The central bank raises the cash deposit ratio to 10%. What will be the outcome?

options.A: Commercial banks will decrease deposits to $500 million.
options.B: Commercial banks will deposit $5 million in the central bank.
options.C: Commercial banks will deposit $10 million in the central bank.
options.D: Commercial banks will increase money in circulation by $5 million.

options.B: constant decrease decrease
options.C: increase decrease increase

questions.questionText: A country decides to abolish its tariff on imports of copper from Zambia. Under which circumstances would this benefit Zambia?

options.A: The income elasticity of demand for copper is greater than one.
options.B: The price elasticity of demand for copper is greater than one.
options.C: The price elasticity of demand for copper is less than one.
options.D: The price elasticity of supply for copper is less than one.

questions.questionText: A small island economy imports most of its raw materials and demand for its exports is price- elastic. What would be the most likely effect of an appreciation of its currency on its balance of payments on the current account and the rate of inflation? balance of payments rate of inflation on the current account

options.B: improves rises
options.C: worsens falls

questions.questionText: What will be most likely to rise if unemployment is increasing in an economy?

options.A: the human capital of unemployed workers
options.B: the living standards of all workers
options.C: the nominal money wage rate of employed workers
options.D: the tax burden on employed workers
